references.text: Moses' hand became leprous and was then healed when God commanded him to stretch it out and draw it back – a parallel to Jesus' command to stretch out the hand and the subsequent healing.
Jeroboam's hand withered and was then restored, an Old Testament parallel to the healing of the withered hand.
Matthew's parallel account of the healing of the man with the withered hand on the Sabbath, where Jesus commands him to stretch out his hand and it is made whole.
Mark's parallel account of the healing of the man with the withered hand in the synagogue on the Sabbath, where Jesus looks around at them with anger and commands the man to stretch out his hand.
The immediate context where Jesus asks whether it is lawful to do good or evil on the Sabbath, leading up to the actual healing in verse 10.
Mark specifically describes that Jesus looked around at them (περιβλεψάμενος) with anger, the same word used in Luke 6:10 about Jesus looking around at all of them.
Another healing where Jesus takes the initiative and heals on the Sabbath – the woman who had been bent double for eighteen years, showing Jesus' consistent practice of healing on the Sabbath.

Jesus commands the sick man by the Pool of Bethesda to get up, take his bed, and walk, and the man was immediately healed – a parallel where Jesus' words alone bring about instant healing, also on the Sabbath.
